Hi Avery / Rachel,

Thanks again for partnering with Redwood. As we discussed on the procurement side, this thread will be our enablement checkpoint for the streaming + function/tool calling + structured outputs work that CuraDx wants to ship in Q4. Goal here is to align on scope, deliverables, and a concrete kickoff agenda so engineering can start model integration and schema validation next week.

High-level objectives for the kickoff
- Confirm output JSON schema and strict/optional fields (prescription object, medication arrays, metadata).
- Map streaming vs batch use-cases and expected latency targets for live triage flows.
- Define function/tool call surface (external medDB lookup, pharmacy API) and security requirements.
- Agree rollout plan and sign-off criteria for feature gates.

Proposed next steps
1) Quick 60-minute kickoff: Wed Oct 7, 10:00 AM PT (suggested) — please confirm.
2) Pre-read items attached: enablement playbook and a small example schema.
3) If you have any mandatory fields for the schema, please reply inline.

Attachments: CuraDx_Enablement_Playbook_v1.2.pdf, schema-example.json
Related links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/92761

If Wed 10:00 PT doesn't work, propose two alternative windows and we'll accommodate.

Thanks,

Thanks Naomi — Wed Oct 7 at 10:00 AM PT works for us. Quick notes from the CuraDx side before the call:
- We have strict schema requirements for the prescription object: prescription.id (uuid), patient_id, medication[] with name, dosage_mg, frequency, start_date, end_date (end_date optional). We can attach our compliance doc.
- Function calls: we expect Redwood to call our pharmacy lookup endpoint (token-based) and return structured results; also need a mapping for error states and retry semantics.
- Streaming expectations: first-token latency target is 250ms on average for 95th percentile. If you have any benchmarks for that in the playbook, please flag.

I attached our curadx_schema_requirements.docx and a short CSV of example records.

See you on Wednesday.

— Avery

On Mon, Oct 5, 2026 at 11:03 AM Avery Lewis <avery.lewis@curadx.com> wrote:
> We have strict schema requirements for the prescription object ...

Thanks for the heads-up Avery — copying a quick technical checklist we'll propose for the kickoff. I'm attaching a small schema-example.json to illustrate the mapping.

Technical kickoff checklist (proposed)
- Schema review (30 min): go field-by-field, mark required vs optional, and decide on validation behavior (strict reject vs best-effort).
- Streaming topology (10 min): clarify stream session lifecycle, KV cache expectations, and prefix caching for repeated prompts.
- Function/tool call spec (10 min): define endpoints, auth (Bearer token), error codes, and idempotency keys.
- E2E test plan & sign-off (10 min): define 3 golden prompts, acceptance criteria, and rollout gates.

Risks & asks ahead of kickoff
- Please confirm the exact field names for medication.* and whether you need units normalized (mg vs mg_int).
- If your pharmacy lookup returns multiple candidates, how should we prioritize? (first match vs score-based).

Attachments: schema-example.json (small, illustrative)

Ben — I'll include the high-level SOW and next-step DocuSign link in my notes so legal/commercial are looped after the kickoff.

Marissa Cole
